brief: Goldman Sachs sector specialist desk note published ahead of the August payrolls release. The desk forecasts nonfarm payrolls of 40k against consensus of +55k, reasoning that big data job growth indicators slowed sequentially and that August initial prints have carried a consistent negative bias for a decade, partly offset by low layoffs and scope for rebounds in leisure and hospitality and local education. It forecasts the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.1%, in line with consensus, on stabilized continuing claims, and average hourly earnings up 0.4% month over month, above consensus, on calendar effects. The desk expects debate over a Fed rate hike to follow the print. Overnight it reports S&P futures stable with technology leading, HSI up 174bps, KOSPI up 164bps, German factory orders at +2.5% versus +0.5% consensus, WTI $91, corn $5.15, the 10 year at 4.76%, DXY $99 and Bitcoin at $81.1k. It flags September seasonality as challenging for industrials. On the micro it reports NX beating on EPS, revenue and EBITDA with the price versus cost imbalance improving, XPO August LTL tonnage up 3.7%, and Tesla opening Cybercab robotaxi rides after 1 million unsupervised miles.
